claims.text: What the strip looks like W an inferior STEMI, suggested by ST elevation in V1 and ST elevation in III more than II; confirmed by ST elevation in the right-sided leads (V3R–V6R).
claims.quote: In patients with inferior STEMI, RV infarction is suggested by: ST elevation in V1 ST elevation in V1 and ST depression in V2 (highly specific for RV infarction) Isoelectric ST segment in V1 with marked ST depression in V2 ST elevation in III > II Diagnosis is confirmed by the presence of ST elevation in the right-sided leads (V3R-V6R)

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) V1 and V2: ST elevation in V1 w ST depression in V2 = highly specific
claims.quote: ST elevation in V1 and ST depression in V2 (highly specific for RV infarction)

claims.text: V4R: the most useful right-sided lead (V4 electrode in the 5th Rt intercostal space, midclav line); ST elevation there has sensitivity 88%, specificity 78%
claims.quote: The most useful lead is V4R, which is obtained by placing the V4 electrode in the 5th right intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line ST elevation in V4R has a sensitivity of 88%, specificity of 78% and diagnostic accuracy of 83% in the diagnosis of RV MI

claims.text: Timing: right-sided ST elevation = transient — it lasts < 10 hrs in 50% of pts
claims.quote: ST elevation in the right-sided leads is a transient phenomenon, lasting less than 10 hours in 50% of patients with RV infarction.

claims.text: Why V1 and III: V1 = the only strd lead looking directly @ the RV; III faces more rightward than II
claims.quote: V1 is the only standard ECG lead that looks directly at the right ventricle Lead III is more rightward facing than lead II and hence more sensitive to the injury current produced by the right ventricle

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) A.: prox RCA (ST elevation in V3R, V4R)
claims.quote: Right ventricular V3R, V4R — Proximal RCA

claims.text: Complicates up to 40% of I. STEMIs; isolated RV infarct = extremely uncommon
claims.quote: RV infarction complicates up to 40% of inferior STEMIs (isolated RV infarction is extremely uncommon)

claims.text: Sx Hypotension may be the first sign, in a previously stable pt
claims.quote: The first sign may be hypotension developing in a patient whose condition had been previously stable.

claims.text: Signs: ↑RV filling P, distended jugular veins (often Kussmaul sign), clear lung fields, hypotension
claims.quote: In right ventricular (RV) infarction, signs include elevated RV filling pressure, distended jugular veins (often with Kussmaul sign), clear lung fields, and hypotension.
claims.locator: Symptoms and Signs of Acute MI

claims.text: Tx Up to 40% of I. MIs involve the RV; nitrates can cause severe hypotension — tx = fluids
claims.quote: Up to 40% of inferior MIs have RV involvement. Missing this is clinically important: nitrates can cause severe hypotension in RV infarct; treatment is fluids.

claims.text: Very preload-sensitive: nitrates or other preload-reducing drugs can cause severe hypotension
claims.quote: These patients are very preload sensitive (due to poor RV contractility) and can develop severe hypotension in response to nitrates or other preload-reducing agents.

claims.text: Fluids: 1–2 L of 0.9% saline = often effective; dobutamine or milrinone may help; ⍉nitrates or diuretics
claims.quote: Volume loading with 1 to 2 L of 0.9% saline is often effective. Dobutamine or milrinone (which has better dilating effects on the pulmonary circulation) may help. Nitrates and diuretics are not used; they reduce preload (and hence cardiac output), causing severe hypotension.
